system.name: BIFROST
system.one_liner: Alibaba's next-generation VPC network providing high-performance multipath reliable transport

components.name: VM1
components.role: a guest VM sending or receiving packets

components.name: vNIC
components.role: buffers a sent packet in VM memory until acknowledged; receives out-of-order placements and in-order notifications on the receive side

components.name: CIPU
components.role: Alibaba's in-house SmartNIC hosting the Hardware Accelerator and Software layers

components.name: Hardware Accelerator
components.role: hosts Bifrost offloading and AVS offloading, connected to the network via Port0/Port1

components.name: Bifrost offloading
components.role: hardware-accelerated path for Bifrost's reliable-transport processing (get pkt, free buf, packet spraying, in-order notification)

components.name: AVS offloading
components.role: hardware-accelerated path for AVS's VPC network forwarding; places out-of-order packets directly into guest VM memory

components.name: Port0
components.role: a physical network port used for multipath packet spraying

components.name: Port1
components.role: a physical network port used for multipath packet spraying

components.name: RT Engine
components.role: the reliable transport engine: sprays packets across paths based on historical RTT, reorders packet metadata, and aggregates ACKs into a bitmap

flows.what: multipath-sprayed packet (vxlan|Bifrost|packet) based on historical RTT
out-of-order packet placement directly into guest VM memory
ACK bitmap reply to sender (vxlan|Bifrost|ACK bitmap)

content.key_idea: Bifrost's CIPU accelerator sprays packets across multiple paths, places out-of-order data directly in guest memory, reorders only metadata, and reports delivery via a delayed ACK bitmap.
content.reading_order: Left panel (sender) and right panel (receiver) mirror each other top-down from VMs to CIPU; nine circled numbers, keyed by the middle legend, trace the send-spray-receive-reorder-ACK sequence.

evidence: Figure 10 illustrates the overview of BIFROST, which integrates several key components
The RTE generates ACKs, which are aggregated into a bitmap and sent to the sender.
OOO packets are placed directly into the guest VM memory...without extra buffering on the CIPU

summary: Figure 10 gives BIFROST's end-to-end overview, drawn as two mirrored diagrams (sender left, receiver right) plus a middle legend. On the sender, a packet flows from the VM's vNIC into the CIPU's Bifrost-offloading hardware (1, get pkt), exchanges metadata with the RT Engine (2), and is sprayed across multiple physical ports as a vxlan|Bifrost|packet based on historical RTT (3); once acknowledged, the buffer is freed (9). On the receiver, out-of-order packets are placed straight into guest VM memory via AVS offloading (4) while the RT Engine reorders only their metadata (5), accumulates ACKs into a bitmap (6), and Bifrost offloading issues an in-order notification to the VM (7); the ACK bitmap is then sent back to the sender (8). Circled numbers tie each arrow to one of Bifrost's four optimizations (multipath spraying, in-place reordering, delayed ACK bitmap, efficient reliability management) listed in the legend.
summary_zh: 图10为BIFROST整体流程：发送端经CIPU的Bifrost offloading获取报文并多路径喷发；接收端由AVS offloading将乱序报文直接放入VM内存，RT Engine重排元数据并聚合ACK位图后按序通知VM。
notes: layout-proposal: mirrored sender/receiver host-device pair - each panel is itself a host-device split (VMs over CIPU), repeated twice with swapped internal box order for sender vs. receiver and tied together by a numbered-step legend in the middle; neither plain host-device nor plain two-panel captures both the internal split and the left/right mirroring at once. Ctrlpath's novelty is unclear from the given text (grouped with the Bifrost-specific RT Engine but could be pre-existing CIPU control-plane software).
